# Results — Study 928 (Odd-Lot Priority) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The trade: an issuer announces
a modified Dutch auction self-tender; the offer is public at the close of day **t**; an
outside buyer takes an odd lot (fewer than 100 shares) at the close of **t+1** — the one
and only execution lag — tenders all of it, is filled **in full** under the odd-lot
priority clause at the clearing price, and is out at expiry. 180 SC TO-I events filed,
178 after the recycled-symbol exclusion, 167 windows fully covered, 2010–2025. Daily
**total-return** closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`), market leg **SPY**, cash leg
**BIL**. As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current month is dropped).*

**Declared PROXIES / ASSUMPTIONS — none of these is on the price tape, and every one is
swept below:** clearing premium **13%** over the pre-announcement close (Comment-Jarrell /
Bagwell mid-range); offer length **21 trading days** (the Rule 14e-1 minimum of 20 business
days, +1); round-lot proration fill **0.35**; broker corporate-action fee **$30** on a
**$5,000** odd lot; one-way cost **15 bps × NAV**; SPY-hedge borrow **40 bps/yr**. The
pre-announcement anchor is the close 6 sessions before commencement; the post-expiry mark
is 5 sessions after expiry.

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | Events | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128 issuer tapes + SPY (market) + BIL (cash) | 2010-01-28 → 2025-11-21 | 167 of 178 usable (10.6/yr) | Fingerprint `4f4dc9efc748` |

The fingerprint is taken over the 167 × 9 matrix of **price marks the study actually uses**
(`p_pre, p_ann, p_entry, p_exp, p_post` and the four SPY marks), not over the whole shared
cache: `studies/_cache` is written by several studies, and a re-fetch of an unrelated
ticker must not move this study's data stamp. Total-return closes are re-adjusted by the
vendor with every new dividend, so the marks drift in the sixth significant figure between
pulls — the stamp moved from `2f3f8b2164fb` to `4f4dc9efc748` across two pulls of the same
window — while everything below, quoted to two decimals, is unchanged.

**Survivorship, named.** The CIK→ticker map is SEC's *current* `company_tickers.json`, so
issuers acquired, taken private or liquidated after their tender carry no ticker and drop
out — and an issuer that went private *because* of the tender is exactly the case where the
post-expiry price would matter most. 180 SC TO-I filings, 178 after excluding a symbol
recycled by a different company post-bankruptcy, **129 distinct issuer tickers of which 128
have a recoverable tape**, and 167 of the 178 events have a fully covered window (the other
11 run off one end of their issuer's tape). Prices are **total-return**, not price-only.
The list is also concentrated in serial repurchasers — PAM Transportation appears 7 times,
White Mountains 5, Tucows 4, InvenTrust 4 — so the event draws are not 178 independent
firms.

## The tape legs — no premium assumption enters the first four

| Leg | Mean | Median | HAC *t* | Hit rate | Bootstrap 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Run-up** *t−6 → t+1* (what the pop takes) | **+7.41%** | +5.94% | **+9.45** | 0.80 | [+5.99, +8.96] |
| Run-up, abnormal (minus SPY) | **+6.87%** | +4.73% | **+9.06** | 0.85 | [+5.47, +8.43] |
| Offer-window drift *t+1 → expiry* | +1.44% | +2.11% | +1.75 | 0.66 | [−0.36, +2.86] |
| **Post-expiry give-back** (5 sessions) | **−0.50%** | +0.00% | **−1.17** | 0.47 | [−1.33, +0.34] |
| Permanent reprice *t−6 → post* | +8.63% | +8.02% | +6.58 | 0.77 | [+6.07, +11.16] |
| Permanent, abnormal | +6.23% | +6.13% | +5.24 | 0.67 | [+3.83, +8.58] |

Two facts decide the study, and they are the only two that no assumption touches.
**(1)** By the close of *t+1* the market has already taken **+7.4%** — a shade over half a
typical low-teens tender premium — with a *t* of +9.5; in 20% of events the run-up alone
exceeds the whole assumed 13% premium. **(2)** The post-expiry give-back that odd-lot
priority feeds on is **statistically absent** (−0.50%, HAC *t* = −1.17, median exactly
0.00%, hit rate 0.47): the stock keeps the premium (+6.2% abnormal, permanently), so the
round-lot holder's un-filled stub is worth roughly what the odd-lot holder's cash is worth.

## The priced round trips — **every** row below carries the assumed premium

| Arm | Mean per event | HAC *t* | Hit rate | Bootstrap 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Odd lot, net of cost and fee | +5.32% | +7.56 | 0.77 | [+3.95, +6.65] |
| **Odd lot, net + SPY-hedged** | **+3.52%** | **+4.32** | 0.70 | [+1.95, +5.05] |
| Round lot, net, prorated at 0.35 | +1.93% | +3.10 | 0.67 | [+0.56, +3.01] |
| **Value of odd-lot priority** | **+3.39%** | +4.33 | 0.68 | [+1.92, +4.94] |

**The value of odd-lot priority is not a measurement.** It is
`(1 − f) × [(p_clear − p_post)/p_entry + cost]` with `p_clear = p_pre × (1 + premium)`, so
it is the *assumed* premium net of the *measured* post-expiry price — it inherits the
assumption exactly as the round trip does, and its sign is bought, not found:

| Assumed clearing premium | 5% | 9% | **13%** | 17% | 21% | 25% |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Value of odd-lot priority | **−1.49%** | +0.95% | **+3.39%** | +5.83% | +8.27% | +10.72% |
| HAC *t* | −1.95 | +1.23 | **+4.33** | +7.34 | +10.27 | +13.12 |

At 9% it does not clear |*t*| = 2; it crosses **zero at an assumed premium of 7.4%**, below
which the entitlement is worth *less* than nothing; and at the tape-fixed breakeven premium
of 10.17% it is worth +1.67% (*t* = +2.15) — a third of the headline. The only
premium-free statement about priority is the negative one: it can only pay the gap between the tender
price and the post-expiry price, and **that gap is the give-back, which is absent**. In
**32%** of events the post-expiry price is *above* the assumed clearing price — there,
priority forced you out of a stock that kept going up.

## The premium-free number — the breakeven premium

The premium at which the costed, SPY-hedged odd-lot round trip merely matches the market.
No *premium* assumption enters it; it is the run-up, the market's move and the frictions.

| Mean | Median | 75th pctile | Events needing more than the assumed 13% |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **10.17%** | 7.93% | 14.56% | **30%** |

**Premium-free is not assumption-free.** The breakeven still inherits (i) the
pre-announcement **anchor**, which fixes `p_pre` — 9.18% at 2 sessions back, 10.17% at the
default 6, **22.62%** at 21; (ii) the assumed **offer length** — 10.12% at 20 trading days,
11.34% at 40; and (iii) the declared **frictions** — 9.04% at zero cost, **12.91%** at $30
plus a 100 bps touch. The anchor is by far the widest of the three and is the single most
fragile choice in the study.

## Premium sweep — the assumption that decides the sign of both arms

| Assumed clearing premium | Hedged round trip | HAC *t* | Hit rate | $ per event ($5,000 lot) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5% | −3.99% | −5.18 | 0.31 | −$199 |
| **9%** | **−0.23%** | **−0.30** | 0.56 | −$12 |
| **13%** (default) | **+3.52%** | **+4.32** | 0.70 | +$176 |
| 17% | +7.27% | +8.68 | 0.81 | +$364 |
| 25% | +14.78% | +16.72 | 0.91 | +$739 |

The sign flips between **9%** and **13%**. The whole *t* = +4.3 is bought with the
assumption; the tape only fixes the breakeven at ~10%.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01, fixed in advance, not searched)

| Era | n | Run-up | Give-back | Hedged round trip (*t*) | Priority value | Breakeven |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010–2017 | 74 | +5.29% | +0.27% | **+5.20%** (*t* = +7.13) | +3.30% | 7.89% |
| 2018–2025 | 93 | **+9.10%** | −1.12% | **+2.19%** (*t* = +1.72) | +3.47% | **11.99%** |

Two point estimates are not a contrast, so the **difference itself is tested** (Welch *t*
on the per-event vectors, late minus early):

| Contrast | Early → late | Gap | Welch *t* | Verdict on the change |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| Run-up | +5.29% → +9.10% | +3.82 pp | **+2.63** | real change |
| Breakeven premium | 7.89% → 11.99% | +4.10 pp | **+2.49** | real change |
| Hedged round trip | +5.20% → +2.19% | −3.01 pp | −1.99 | **below the bar** |
| Give-back | +0.27% → −1.12% | −1.39 pp | −1.77 | below the bar |
| Priority value | +3.30% → +3.47% | +0.16 pp | +0.11 | no change |

Said precisely: **what has demonstrably changed is the entry price, not the profit.** The
run-up has grown and the breakeven premium with it, both clearing |*t*| = 2 as *changes*.
The fall in the hedged round trip from +5.20% to +2.19% is what that implies, but the
decline is *itself* a *t* = −1.99 result and does not clear the bar — so "the margin is
being arbitraged away" is a statement supported on the entry-price leg and only suggested
on the profit leg. What is not in doubt is the level: post-2018 the round trip runs at
*t* = +1.72, which does not clear 2 on its own, and the breakeven has reached 11.99% —
within a point of the premium the study assumes.

## Sweeps over every other assumption

**Proration** (what priority is worth; 1.00 = under-subscribed, priority worthless) — note
that the HAC *t* is **invariant** at +4.33 across this whole row, because `priority_value`
scales linearly in `(1 − f)`: the proration factor sets the size, the *premium* sets the
sign and the significance.

| Round-lot fill | Priority value | Round-lot round trip |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.15 | +4.44% | +0.89% |
| 0.35 | +3.39% | +1.93% |
| 0.75 | +1.31% | +4.02% |
| **1.00** | **+0.00%** | +5.32% |

**Cost** — the flat corporate-action fee is one live cost; the bps touch is the other, and
it is charged **three times** per hedged round trip (the odd-lot purchase plus the SPY
hedge's own round trip). The grid runs to 100 bps because a third of this event list is
micro-cap (Socket Mobile, Optex, Mannatech, Bimini, IZEA, Wheeler), where the touch on 99
shares is nothing like the 15 bps default:

| Fee / one-way bps | 0 bps | 15 bps | 40 bps | 100 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| $0 | +4.57% | +4.12% | +3.37% | +1.57% (*t* = +1.93) |
| $30 | +3.97% | **+3.52%** | +2.77% | **+0.97%** (*t* = +1.19) |
| $50 | +3.57% | +3.12% | +2.37% (*t* = +2.91) | +0.57% (*t* = +0.70) |

**This is the second way the headline dies.** At a $30 fee and a 100 bps touch — a fair
description of buying 99 shares of a micro-cap — the hedged round trip is +0.97% with
*t* = +1.19, and the breakeven premium rises to **12.91%**, i.e. all the way to the premium
the study assumed. The headline *t* = +4.3 needs both a 13% clearing premium **and** a
liquid-name touch.

**Capacity** — a 99-share lot is 99 × the share price and nothing more:

| Odd-lot position | Hedged round trip | HAC *t* | $ per event | $ per year (10.6 events) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| $1,000 (99 sh @ $10) | +1.12% | +1.37 | $11 | **$118** |
| $2,500 | +2.92% | +3.58 | $73 | $771 |
| $5,000 (default) | +3.52% | +4.32 | $176 | **$1,859** |
| $9,900 (99 sh @ $100) | +3.82% | +4.68 | $378 | $3,990 |

**Borrow** on the short SPY hedge: +3.55% at 0 bps → +3.30% at 300 bps (*t* = +4.05). The
hedge is cheap; borrow is not what decides this study. **Offer length** (assumed, not
observed): 20 td +3.56% (*t* = +4.36) → 40 td +2.42% (*t* = +2.52). **Anchor** for the
pre-announcement price: 2 sessions back +4.21% (*t* = +5.92), 6 sessions (default) +3.52%,
21 sessions +2.15% (*t* = +1.98, breakeven 22.6%).

## Calendar-time sleeve, excess-of-cash — the un-achievable scaled version

Equal-weight across live positions, cash (BIL) when idle, both arms minus BIL, 2010-02-01 →
2025-12-23 (4,000 sessions, invested on 51.9% of them, 1.61 live names on average). This
version applies the **odd-lot fill assumption at portfolio scale** — precisely what the
odd-lot rule forbids — and it also carries the **13% clearing premium** (the tender payoff
`p_clear / p_exp − 1` lands on the expiry session). It is quoted only to show that even the
doubly-assumed fantasy version does not win the risk-adjusted race.

| | Sleeve excess Sharpe | SPY excess Sharpe | Advantage | HAC *t* on the daily difference | Sleeve vol |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Gross | +0.787 | +0.799 | −0.012 | +2.40 | 65.9% |
| **Net** | **+0.715** | +0.799 | **−0.084** | +2.09 | 65.6% |

The sleeve earns a *higher mean* than SPY (hence the positive difference *t* = +2.09) and a
*lower Sharpe*, because holding 1.6 single names at full weight runs at **66% annualised
volatility**. The positive mean is not evidence for the trade — it is the same assumed
premium, paid at a scale the rule prohibits. A concentrated single-name sleeve that loses
the Sharpe race is not a diversifier and not an allocation.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof — never supports the stamp)

| World | Run-up recovered | Give-back recovered | Breakeven |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Planted (+500 bps run-up, −400 bps give-back) | **+466 bps** (*t* = +10.42) | **−387 bps** (*t* = −9.93) | 5.45% |
| Null (nothing planted) | −44 bps (*t* = −1.04) | +6 bps (*t* = +0.14) | 0.30% |
| Null × 8 seeds | mean +43 bps (sd 70), \|*t*\| ≥ 2 in **1/8** | mean +27 bps, \|*t*\| ≥ 2 in **0/8** | — |

The estimator recovers a planted run-up and a planted give-back and stays quiet on the
null. The absent post-expiry give-back on the real tape is therefore a fact about tenders,
not a broken harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Mixed.** The split is by **leg**, and it is a split between what the tape
  says and what an assumption says. **Real on the announcement run-up:** the market takes
  **+7.41%** (abnormal +6.87%, HAC *t* = +9.06) of a low-teens premium before an outside
  buyer can act, and in 20% of events the pop alone exceeds the whole assumed premium. That
  number needs no proxy. **None on the post-expiry give-back** — the leg the odd-lot claim
  actually depends on: −0.50%, HAC *t* = −1.17, median exactly 0.00%, hit rate 0.47. The
  stock keeps the premium (+6.2% abnormal, permanently), so the stub the round-lot holder
  keeps is worth about what the odd-lot holder's cash is worth, and in 32% of events it is
  worth more. Every profitable number in this study — the +3.52% hedged round trip
  (*t* = +4.32) **and** the +3.39% "value of priority" (*t* = +4.33) alike — is the assumed
  13% clearing premium meeting the tape: both flip sign inside the swept grid, the round
  trip between 9% and 13% and priority at 7.4%. The premium-free summary statistic is the
  breakeven, **10.17%** (median 7.93%), which post-2018 has risen to **11.99%** — a rise
  that is itself significant (Welch *t* = +2.49) — and which reaches **12.91%** once a
  micro-cap 100 bps touch is charged, at which point the round trip is +0.97% with
  *t* = +1.19. Not Real: the only legs clearing |*t*| = 2 without a proxy are the run-up
  and the permanent reprice, neither of which is the claim. Not None: those legs are
  measured at *t* ≈ 9 and they are what kills the folklore.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** The rule that creates the edge also caps it: 99 shares. At the
  default assumptions the trade is **$176 per event, ~$1,859 a year** before tax, per
  account — and **$118 a year** on a $10 stock, where the flat broker fee alone is 300 bps
  and the HAC *t* falls to +1.37. The $10 case is not a corner: cheap shares are exactly
  where the odd-lot allowance buys the least, and they are also where the 100 bps touch
  applies. The only version with real dollars in it is the round-lot version, which is
  exactly the version proration hits. Scaling it is not a capital problem but a *legal*
  one, and the scaled fantasy sleeve loses the excess-of-cash Sharpe race to SPY
  (**+0.715 vs +0.799**) at 66% volatility. Nothing here is bankable at desk size.
